decisions.statement: The reading is taken on the workstation with the checkout.
The grams are kept beside the readout the grams were counted for.
The question to ask and how to read the answer are on the readout's own page.
The grams are a sum over food entries rather than a field on a tracking day.
The day a food entry counts to is worked out from the instant that entry happened at.
The checkout is asked directly rather than through the module saying where a day is kept.
A food entry is asked for as an akasha page rather than through the markdown client.
A checkout's refusal is an answer that is not ok rather than a throw.
A run of this file takes a reading.
The root read is the root the environment states or the folder the call was made in.
An empty value in the environment states no root.
Where the readout's page sits is asked of the index rather than spelled.
The grams themselves are never printed.
Importing this file takes no reading.
Nothing here decides when a reading is due.

definition: the grams of whole plants Alan ate, counted from his food entries and kept on the readout
